findings.issue: Whether the chain owns the Docker engine is decided by one `docker ps` probe at the night's start. The code's own comment at :287 says one failed probe does not mean the engine is down, yet that single probe decides ownership. Failure path: the owner's engine (with the supabase stack) is up all night, the start probe fails once, and the engine later misses the three probes at the Linux lanes. container_up then runs `docker desktop start`, sets cs_started=1 when it returns 0, and container_down runs `docker desktop stop`. That stops the owner's engine, which D56(g) and the owner's directive forbid.
findings.evidence: Added a harness case X1 in a scratch copy: a docker stub fails `ps` calls 1, 3, 4 and 5, and `desktop start` returns 0 as if the engine were already running. Result: FAIL. chain.log shows 'engine up at start=0', then 'docker engine not answering (3 probes): starting it', then 'engine started by this chain', 'container start exit=0', 'container stopped exit=0' and 'engine stopped exit=0'. The case's check 'the owner's engine (up all night) is never stopped' failed. The existing O15 only injects a failure at the Linux-lanes probe, not at the start probe.
findings.fix: Take engine_up_at_start from docker_answers (three probes), the same rule as elsewhere. Set cs_started=1 only when `docker desktop status`, read before the start, said the engine was stopped. Never `docker desktop stop` while containers other than qompack-v6-linux-verification are running. Add X1 as a harness case.

findings.location: plans/sdd/V6-closeout/coordinator/nightharness.sh:22-23 (T=$(mktemp -d), HB=$T/bin) and :1536 (PATH="$HB:$PATH"); claims at nightharness.sh:9-18 and README.md:29
findings.issue: The dry harness has no guard that its stubs are actually on PATH. When TMPDIR is a Windows-form path (for example a Claude Code scratchpad written as C:/...), mktemp returns C:/..., and PATH="C:/...bin:$PATH" splits at the drive colon. Every stub (docker, powershell, go, gh, timeout, date, sleep) is then bypassed, and the copied night scripts run against the real tools. The header's claim ('nothing outside its temporary directory is touched ... starts no Docker, Claude Code or Go process') then does not hold. N cases could also reach the real gh if the real clock passed their deadline check.
findings.evidence: My first run (TMPDIR=C:/Users/Quant/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/qompack-audit2/night/tmp) gave U1-U3 FAIL and O1 'REFUSED: the deadline 2026-10-05T08:00:00 is more than 16 h away', because the real date was used. Later cases ran overnight-c8.sh against the REAL docker. Their chain.log files (O19, O25, O26, O27, O31) show 'engine up at start=1', the owner's supabase_* containers listed, then 'container start exit=0' / 'container stopped exit=0' on the real qompack-v6-linux-verification, and release-check clones with a real `go run`. With TMPDIR=/c/... and a guard that checks `command -v docker` resolves to $HB/docker, the same cases pass. Side effect, disclosed: the night container was started and stopped repeatedly; it is now 'Exited (137)' with NanoCpus 8e9, Memory 8 GiB and MemorySwap 8 GiB (the values the night sets). The owner's engine was never stopped (engine up at start=1).
findings.fix: In nightharness.sh, after HB is created, use T=$(cygpath -u "$(mktemp -d)") (or refuse a T containing ':'). Inside each case subshell, refuse to run unless `command -v` resolves docker, gh, go, powershell, pwsh, timeout, date and sleep to $HB/<name>. Make the README's claim conditional on that guard.

findings.location: plans/sdd/V6-closeout/coordinator/c8-night.sh:73 (trap 'exit 143' TERM) and overnight-c8.sh:249; harness cases N9 and O9
findings.issue: sh defers a trapped signal until the current foreground child exits. A TERM sent to the night shell during the pre-freeze (up to 60-90 min a step) or release-check (about 3 h) therefore deletes the sentinel, stops the keep-awake and removes the scratch clone only after that whole step ends, and the step keeps running. N9 and O9 release the blocked stub (echo go > go.fifo) right after the kill, so they cannot observe the deferral. The header's 'released on every way out ... a catchable signal' holds only after that delay.
findings.evidence: Probe: sh script with `trap 'echo trap ran at $(date +%s); exit 143' TERM`, then `/usr/bin/sleep 8`. Output: start 1791126208, TERM sent 1791126210, 'trap ran at 1791126216' (after the sleep), rc=143.
findings.fix: Run long children as `cmd & wait $!`; wait is interruptible, so the trap runs at once and can kill the child's process group. Or state in the header and README that only nightabort.ps1 stops the night promptly and that its manual steps 2-5 apply.

findings.issue: summary.log's header records `go=$(go env GOVERSION)`, run in the caller's working directory, not in <repo>. go.mod has `toolchain go1.26.6` with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, so a launch from outside a module (Start-Process from a PowerShell window in C:\Users\Quant) records the local default toolchain, while every step runs on go1.26.6.
findings.evidence: `cd /c/Users/Quant && go env GOVERSION GOTOOLCHAIN` gives go1.26.4 and auto. `cd qompack-cx-int && go env GOVERSION` gives go1.26.6. c8-night.sh invokes prefreeze.sh before any cd, so the cwd is the launch cwd. The harness's go stub answers go1.26.6 to every call, so it cannot catch this.
findings.fix: `go=$(cd "$R" && go env GOVERSION)`. Optionally log the same in overnight-c8.sh's start line from the candidate checkout.

findings.issue: The night judges all of test/e2e in one binary under a 30-minute timeout, and the recorded margin is about 15%. A timeout is a VALID red (failed=1, so the live re-check is blocked) and says nothing about wall-clock budgets. Candidate 8 adds test/e2e work (113 to 114 test functions, X10 +24 lines, X14 +19 lines), and earlier runs of this package have hit the 1800 s wall.
findings.evidence: phase3/c5/p3-win-e2e-timing.log:184 'FAIL ... test/e2e 1513.749s'; phase3/c6/p3-win-e2e-timing.log:145 '1529.497s' (84-85% of 1800 s). Earlier timeouts: e2e/runs/pkg-test-e2e-windows.log:256 and hostperm/runs/94-e2e-full-windows.log:304, both '1800.4s'. Wave 21's quiet e2efunc took 08:06-08:19Z (13 min) without X11. X11 alone took 5m50s on c5 and 10m54s on c6.
findings.fix: Measure test/e2e's whole-package time on candidate 8 on AC before the night. If it is above about 1600 s, give the local win-e2e-timing lane a longer -timeout (no judgement changes) and update the harness's exact-line check at nightharness.sh:1392. Otherwise record the margin in the README.

findings.issue: Four timing risks at the end of candidate 8's night. (1) RC_EST_S (3 h) has never been measured on this tree: release-check has never run locally with its current step list (lint with stubskips' whole-tree pass, test, cover, build-all, guards, govulncheck, determinism, rollback, plugin-validate, marketplace). Nothing stops it at the deadline, so an overrun lands in the owner's day. (2) release-check is not AC-gated at its start, and in this night no retry can fit, because try 1 ends about at the deadline. Given the charger's cut pattern, one AC event in either test/e2e window voids C3.12 / D57(a) for the night. (3) Gated steps without an estimate (win-e2e-timing about 26 min, c51-linux with its container start) may start just before the deadline and run past it.
findings.evidence: `grep -rl '=== release-check: ci-local test ===' plans/` finds nothing. w17-release/report.md:103 bases its estimate on SP-17's 8451 s 'before the marketplace step existed and on a smaller tree'. The System log over the last 3 days (power_events_since) shows on-AC stretches of 1h15m, 1h26m, 2h06m, 2h57m and 6h06m. The AC was cut again at about 11:20 today (BAT 85). In run_gated, g_est is empty for win-*, c51-* steps.
findings.fix: Time one release-check --tag run in a scratch clone on AC before relying on RC_EST_S, or add a watchdog that stops release-check at the deadline plus a grace period, logging it as SKIPPED-OVERRUN. Let release-check wait for AC up to its latest start (deadline minus RC_EST_S) when it is on battery. Give win-e2e-timing, win-x11-alone and c51-* estimates from candidate 6's records.

findings.issue: Every power reading and event query runs `powershell -Command` with no time bound, and each step makes at least two of these calls. A hung WMI or PowerShell query stalls the chain with nothing to stop it, past the deadline and into the owner's day, with the keep-awake still held. Docker, git push and gh calls are all wrapped in timeout; this one is not.
findings.evidence: `power_ps() { powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$1" 2>&1 | tr -d '\r'; }`. Measured now under load: power_read 0.795 s ('BAT 85'), power_events_since over 1 h 2.754 s, so a 60-120 s bound costs nothing.
findings.fix: `timeout -k 10 120 powershell ...`. A timed-out power_read reads 'UNKNOWN ?', and a timed-out power_events_since returns 1 (unreadable, so NOT-REFERENCE), which the parsers already handle.

findings.issue: The script refuses a deadline that is too far away but has no check for one that is too near. A launch for example 30 minutes before NIGHT_DEADLINE passes deadline_near, runs the 1 h pre-freeze, and then still freezes and pushes candidate 8 in the morning, with every overnight step SKIPPED. That uses up the freeze without any night evidence. README says to launch 8.5 h before the deadline, but nothing checks it or warns.
findings.evidence: deadline_near only tests `deadline - now <= NIGHT_MAX_AHEAD_H*3600`. Harness N14 (NIGHT_DEADLINE=22:10, launch at 22:00) passes with 'every step SKIPPED', and in that case the freeze and push still happen.
findings.fix: At start, log 'WARNING: release-check will be SKIPPED' when now + 4.25 h + RC_EST_S > deadline, and refuse when now + 1.5 h > deadline unless NIGHT_ALLOW_LATE=1.

findings.issue: The keep-awake is started and its pid logged, but the night never confirms it holds. If pwsh is missing from the detached environment's PATH, or keepawake.ps1 fails, the night runs without a keep-awake request. A host sleep would then void steps; INVALID-POWER records it, but only after the fact.
findings.evidence: keepawake.ps1's output goes to $E8/keepawake.log, which c8-night.sh never reads. The 'start pid ... keep-awake pid $kp' line is logged unconditionally.
findings.fix: Poll keepawake.log for up to 15 s for 'keep-awake held'. Log a WARNING, or refuse, if it does not appear.

findings.issue: Nothing documents how to recover from a refusal after the freeze, at the bundle build or at host validation ('unverified' or 'rejected'). A relaunch of c8-night.sh refuses because qompack-bundles/c8 exists. README's post-freeze path, running the overnight part alone, never host-validates the bundles, pushes verify/v6 or dispatches nightly.yml, so the live re-check's gates (bundle with BUNDLE.json, hosted ci.yml and nightly green) cannot be met by following the README.
findings.evidence: Added harness case X3: kv hv_outcome unverified, run the night, then set accepted and run it again. night.log: 'REFUSED: host validation outcome is 'unverified', not accepted ...', then on relaunch 'REFUSED: .../qompack-bundles/c8 already exists'. The origin has no verify/v6.
findings.fix: Add an Abort step for 'frozen, not pushed': delete the unvalidated qompack-bundles/c8, rebuild and host-validate it from the candidate worktree, push verify/v6 and dispatch nightly.yml, then run the overnight part alone. Alternatively add a C8_RESUME_AFTER_FREEZE mode to c8-night.sh that starts at step 5's bundle build.

findings.issue: release-check's govulncheck step fails outright when the vulnerability database cannot be reached (rcFailf). prefreeze.sh's vuln_check reads the same condition as GOVULNCHECK-UNREACHABLE and does not fail on it. A network blip at night therefore shows up as a VALID red, 'failed=1 [release-check]', with no label, and the steps after it (licenses, determinism, rollback, plugin-validate, marketplace) never run.
findings.evidence: releaseCheckVulncheck: `if err := pinnedRunInherit(govulncheckPkg, "./..."); err != nil { return rcFailf(...) }`. overnight-c8.sh counts any VALID non-zero exit as a fail (:706).
findings.fix: After a red release-check, grep its log for the unreachable pattern that prefreeze.sh uses and record 'release-check: govulncheck unreachable (network), not a product red' in the step's note.

findings.issue: Tonight's live re-check (C4.5) requires two `qompack doctor --json` reads, and two `status --json` reads, to 'agree exactly'. They never do: status always differs in data.collected_at_ms (and the text header 'collected <time>'), and once metrics/latency.json is persisted, doctor --json differs in delivery.rollover's 'persisted Ns ago'. The candidate 7 lane happened to note these as observations. A strict reading of the c8 prompt fails C4.5 on a correct build.
findings.evidence: Probe TestZZAudit2_RealClockReadsAgree on the real clock with a live daemon and two sessions, reads 1.5 s apart: 'status --json: 1 differing lines' (collected_at_ms 1791125313041 vs 1791125314575); 'status: 1 differing lines' (header); doctor --json 0. Probe TestZZAudit2_DoctorAfterPersist (metrics persisted): 'doctor --json: 1 differing lines', with detail '...metrics/latency.json (persisted 1276h19m45s ago)...' vs '...47s ago...'. rerun-c7/C4.5/notes.txt:10-11 and :27-28 record the same differences.
findings.fix: Either make doctor print an absolute time ('persisted at <RFC3339>') so that two doctor --json reads of unchanged state are byte-identical, or reword mkrecheck8.py:167 to exempt data.collected_at_ms, the status 'collected' header and doctor's persisted age explicitly. The first is cleaner and is a non-bundle-neutral code change, so the second is the pre-freeze option.

nits.location: plans/sdd/V6-closeout/coordinator/README.md:85-89; nightharness.sh O1 checks 'the clone path is logged' / 'the clone is removed'
nits.issue: (a) README says the harness takes up to about 2 hours. Under today's load it ran at about 20 cases an hour: 36 cases took about 1 h 40 min, so a sequential 86-case run would take about 4 h. (b) O1's sed `release-check clone \([^ ]*\) at` cannot parse a scratch path that contains a space. 'The clone is removed' then tests `test ! -e ""` and passes vacuously.

So the night scripts themselves handle spaces in paths; only the harness's parse does not. Timing: U, K and O1-O29 (36 cases) took about 1 h 40 min; N3-N22 (20 cases) about 37 min in parallel.
nits.fix: State the time as load-dependent (2-4 h), or split the harness across processes. Parse the clone path with `sed -n 's/^release-check clone \(.*\) at [0-9a-f]\{40\}:.*/\1/p'` and require it to be non-empty before the removal check.
